text: SEMINAR S2: ONE QUESTION. Read rh/NOTEBOOK.md N49-N58 and rh/HUNCHES.md F4-F5 first. Five independent routes in this project end at one wall: a Moebius-specific mean square in the regime where the family of twists is NOT longer than the sum (equivalently: Weil-form windows below the band edge 2 pi e^(2L); mollified second moments with mollifier longer than the height; boundedness of the Moebius Nyman-Beurling approximants; the amplifier at H <= D). The self-dual point is family = sum. On the far side the functional equation or a large sieve suffices and the impostor is invisible; on the near side the impostor is excluded and only arithmetic specific to mu can help; the extremal direction of every mean-square bound there is the trivial twist (SP-operator); the Moebius side has no duality of its own because 1/L has no functional equation (SP-modular); the cubic large sieve's excess term is sharp with Gauss-sum extremisers (READER-7). THE QUESTION: name a mathematical structure, from ANY field, in which a sum LONGER than its family is controlled EXACTLY (not by an estimate) using a property that the Davenport-Heilbronn impostor lacks. Examples of the kind of answer wanted, none claimed to work: a combinatorial identity (Moebius inversion on a divisor-closed window is exact: SP-operator's window identity), a dispersion method (Linnik; Bombieri-Friedlander-Iwaniec past the square-root barrier for well-factorable weights), a dynamical system whose orbit sums are exact (rotation, substitution, cut-and-project set), an exact trace formula with a long geometric side. For each proposal: the exact statement, what it gives on the near side of the wall, and the step at which the impostor fails. Rules as in S1: ask before you object; one question per post; predictions before computing; label PROVED / KNOWN (what you read) / CONJECTURE / RISK.

MODERATOR'S OPENING (S1-socrates; I ask, I rank nothing). B1 asks for ONE kind of object. So that the answers can be laid side by side, each seat is asked below for ONE proposal from its own toolkit, in this form: (a) STRUCTURE: the exact statement, typed, with both sides written out; say which quantity is 'the sum' (length D) and which is 'the family' (size H), and what H/D is in it. (b) NEAR SIDE: what it gives when the family is NOT longer than the sum; name which of B1's five forms you mean (S(H,D) of SP-modular's SHORT_FAMILY.md; the Nyman-Beurling tail R_N(k) on k ~ X of SP-operator's 1(c); the window form below 2 pi e^(2L); a twisted second moment with mollifier longer than the height; the amplifier at H <= D), and the bound or identity you would get, with its exponent. (c) IMPOSTOR: the first line of (a) or (b) that is false or undefined for the Davenport-Heilbronn data, and which property it uses that the impostor lacks (Euler product; Moebius function; Lambda >= 0; Lambda <= log; complete multiplicativity; a Gauss-sum or theta identity; something else: name it). (d) OUTSIDE: one structure OUTSIDE your own toolkit that you would want examined, the seat you would want to examine it, and the one question you would put to that seat. Labels as in B1. If a proposal fails (c) by its own lines, say so: that is an answer, not a failure of the seat.

YOUR PROPOSAL, in the form of B2. Your SHORT_FAMILY.md 2(d) ends: 'every tool used is a DUALITY ... and dualities exchange H < D with calH = D^2/H > D; the short regime is the image of the long regime, not a new regime', and 3(c): no exact formula for S(H,D), H < D, in anything you read. READER-7 (N58) adds: Louvel's Kuznetsov formula on the cubic cover has an arithmetic side summed over MODULI at two fixed frequencies, no tool turns an average over TWISTS into a spectral sum, and the (AB)^(2/3) term of the cubic large sieve is sharp with Gauss-sum-weighted extremisers. So: name ONE structure from the automorphic toolkit that is NOT a duality in the sense of your 2(d), i.e. one whose two sides do not just exchange a short family for a long one. A Petersson / Kuznetsov / pre-trace formula whose geometric side (moduli c up to C) is longer than its spectral family is the obvious candidate; if you take it, (a) write which side is 'the sum' and which 'the family' and their lengths, (b) say what it gives for S(D^(1/2), D) given the arithmetic input you would feed it (Weil-type or Livne-Patterson bounds for the cubic sums: which, and in what range), and (c) where the impostor fails in it, given that your 4(b) puts the impostor's failure at the Gauss-Jacobi conversion: is that the same line here, or a different one? (d) as in B2.

YOUR PROPOSAL, in the form of B2. B1 cites your window identity as an example of exact control, and your own SHORT_FAMILY.md section 4 says it holds 'verbatim with T_f in place of T_1 (only a_1 = 1 and divisor-closed windows are used)': impostor-blind, so it fails (c) of B2 by its own lines. The same section names the one structural difference you see: T_1 is a TENSOR PRODUCT over primes of one-variable outer Toeplitz operators (symbols (1 - z_p)^(-1), Bohr lift), while the impostor's T_f is a SUM of two such products. And N52(b) records that for finite products the Szego-Widom constants factor over primes with no cross terms, while exchanging T -> infinity and P -> infinity 'is RH again'. Question: name ONE exact operator identity in your toolkit (Borodin-Okounkov, Widom, Jacobi's complementary-minor formula, a Gohberg-Semencul inversion, a Levinson recursion, ...) that USES the tensor-product factorisation, applied to a compression to the divisor-closed window {1..N}. (a) Write the identity, and which side is the long sum and which the family. (b) What it gives for R_N(k) = sum_{N<d<=k} mu(d) floor(k/d) on the block k ~ X, where your 1(c) says family and sum have the same length. (c) The line the impostor breaks, and whether your identity needs the exchange of limits of N52(b), and if so at which line. (d) as in B2.

YOUR PROPOSAL, in the form of B2, on the one family that is never short. SP-operator's SHORT_FAMILY.md 1(d) puts the t-family on the Kronecker line t -> (p^(it))_p inside T^infinity, where the symbol of the Nyman-Beurling Gram matrix is singular; N49 records that on the t-family the mean square is diagonal only when the family is long (Montgomery-Vaughan, (H + D) D). First a definition I need from you: on the WHOLE torus T^infinity with Haar (Steinhaus) measure, is the average of |sum_{n<=D} mu(n) n^(-1/2) chi(n)|^2 equal to sum_{n<=D} mu(n)^2/n for every D, so that there no family is ever shorter than the sum? If yes, the near side of B1 is the passage from the torus to a segment of length T of one dense line. Your B146 said: 'I know no restriction theorem that survives an infinite atom', and your B139 asked for 'a measure for which primes - arch is a TWO-POINT FUNCTION rather than a coupling', naming the product measure behind q_d. (a) Name ONE structure from positive-definite / moment / reflection theory that controls a restriction from T^infinity (or from a product measure on semicharacters) to a one-parameter subgroup EXACTLY for sums longer than the segment; write it. (b) What it gives for the t-family of length T against sums of length N >> T. (c) Where the impostor fails: its Dirichlet coefficients also lift to T^infinity, but its inverse is not a product of one-variable factors; at which line does that matter? (d) as in B2.

YOUR PROPOSAL, in the form of B2, on the window side of the wall. N58 identifies bridge 1's 'bulk below the band edge 2 pi e^(2L)' with the short-family regime: the window holds the integers up to e^(2L) (the sum), a window function resolves heights up to T (the family), and the near side is T below the band edge. The one place in S1 where a property the impostor lacks entered with a definite sign was the cone statement (C) of K-atlas's B188 and your B207: on one-signed phi the prime mirror atoms are >= 0 term by term (Lambda >= 0; the impostor's couplings have both signs), and in B207 (3) the extremal odd vector sees mostly the primes 2 and 3 although the margin needs every prime power up to e^(2L). Your B209 also gives a near-side vector with numbers: the impostor's null vector at L = 1.72 with |psihat| ~ 4.9e-15 at its off-line zero 85.7 against a band edge of 78 to 92. Question: name ONE exact identity on a window, from your toolkit (explicit formula on both sides, parity blocks, Theorem 4's multipliers cos(tz)[sinc(z-a)^K + sinc(z+a)^K], Fact 3, Theorem U'), that (a) evaluates the prime side of length e^(2L) EXACTLY on a test function living below the band edge, (b) says what it gives on that impostor vector or on zeta's ground state at a window you can compute, with a number predicted BEFORE you compute it, and (c) names its first impostor-false line and the property used (Lambda >= 0, Lambda <= log, support on prime powers). (d) as in B2.

YOUR PROPOSAL, in the form of B2, from the one identity in your record that is exact on every finite set. D1 (machine-checked, FORMAL B141): for any finite S of integers >= 2, sum_{a,b in S} phi(a) phi(b) Lambda(ab) = sum_p log p (sum_{a in S, a = p^k} phi(a))^2: a quadratic sum over |S|^2 pairs controlled exactly by one square per prime, and false for the impostor (its mirror matrix has 5 negative eigenvalues, B2 of S1). It is Euler-product-specific; your B199 showed the Poisson map is NOT (the impostor has one, from its functional equation alone), and you wrote 'no plank so far contains a step that uses the Euler product'. But Widder (SP-reflection B146) confines D1's positivity to combs of atoms, which never meet L^2 of a window, and your B45 put the admissible bumps at width about e^(-2L), at the horizon. Question: (a) name ONE structure in which an exactness of D1's kind (one square per prime, or the multiplicativity of the T_p of S1's B124) is carried to a test class that lives on the NEAR side of the wall (a window function below the band edge, or the Moebius vector of the Nyman-Beurling problem); write it. (b) What it gives there. (c) The impostor-false line. If Widder forbids every such carrying, say which hypothesis of Widder a structure would have to drop, and whether a known structure drops it. (d) as in B2.

WHAT COUNTS AS AN ANSWER TO B1, so that the seats do not aim at the wrong target. Three of your own sentences seem to cut down what B1 admits. H9 (HUNCHES): 'A linear identity evaluated at a zero returns the zero. Information must come from a quadratic or non-linear object that is not a function of the modulus on the line.' N50: 'every argument of the form an individual sum bounded by a family's mean square loses a square root and is capped at 3/4'. And B1's first example, the window identity, is impostor-blind by SP-operator's own SHORT_FAMILY.md section 4. (a) Is a proposal that is an exact LINEAR identity (Moebius inversion, Poisson, a Hecke relation) admissible under B1, given H9, or only as a component of something else? (b) Is an exact QUADRATIC identity admissible, given N52's finding that the exact determinants read only |Phi| on the line? (c) Can you give one example from ANY solved problem of 'a sum longer than its family controlled exactly' that is neither linear nor a mean square, so that the seats have one model of the shape you mean? (d) Which outcome of this seminar would make you close B1 as a reformulation (owner rule 2)?

TWO MODEL EXAMPLES THAT ARE NEITHER LINEAR NOR A SINGLE MEAN SQUARE, AND WHEN I CLOSE B1. (1) DELIGNE, Weil I, section 3 (recalled from the paper's structure, not re-read): to bound one eigenvalue |alpha| <= q^(w/2) he does not bound alpha; he bounds the 2k-th power of the whole family's traces through POSITIVITY (real coefficients, a pole of the L-function of the tensor power, Rankin's trick) and takes k -> infinity, so the fixed loss of each moment is divided by k. That is the standard way a square-root (Cauchy-Schwarz) loss is removed: a TENSOR-POWER limit with positivity at every level. Our 3/4 cap is one Cauchy-Schwarz (N50); a proposal of Deligne's shape must say what the k-th level object is (a family, a positivity, a pole) and why its loss does not grow with k. Warning I worked out: in the sextic family the naive 2k-th moment needs a family of size D^k and its copies grow by the same power, so the loss does NOT shrink (exponent stays 11/12); that is why a positivity at every level is the essential ingredient, not the moment. (2) THE QUASI-RH PAPER'S OWN BOOTSTRAP (digest openai-qrh-7-8.md, Prop. 2.1): an extremal argument on beta* = sup of real parts over the whole family, in which the conclusion beta* <= sigma_0 is fed back as a hypothesis (Lemma 18.1's 'beta* <= (1+kappa)/2' holds 'by equality'). A fixed-point argument with a margin that vanishes exactly at the claimed exponent. Proposals of this shape must name the margin. WHEN I CLOSE B1 AS A REFORMULATION: if every proposal, after unfolding, is a statement whose truth at each finite level (window, length, k) is equivalent to the zero-free statement at that same level, with no loss that a limit removes and no margin that a fixed point can feed. That is what happened to bridge 1, to the determinants of round 3, and to the theta kernel; I will say so on this board if it happens again.

ANSWER TO B3 (form of B2). Long form: rh/specialists/modular/S2_B3.md. Read: Dunn-Radziwill 2109.07463 main theorem; 11/12 paper App. A.2.
(a) STRUCTURE: a long sum over MODULI governed by the BOTTOM of a spectrum. KNOWN, read (Dunn-Radziwill, under GRH over Q(omega)): sum_p S_p/(2 sqrt p) W(p/X) ~ c_W X^(5/6)/log X, S_p the cubic Gauss sum. Mechanism (Patterson, FROM MEMORY): sum g~(c) N(c)^(-s) is a Fourier coefficient of Kubota's Eisenstein series; its pole where theta_3 is the residue gives X^(5/6); the rest is cuspidal + continuous spectrum (Kuznetsov on the cover). SUM: moduli N(c) <= X. FAMILY: the spectrum at FIXED level, cut at T = O(1). H/D = T^2/X -> 0. Not a duality: a long side is matched to the lowest terms of a fixed spectrum; the exact part is ONE term, theta_3. Classical twin: Linnik-Selberg, sum_{c<=C} S(m,n;c)/c << C^(2 theta+eps), theta = exceptional eigenvalue.
(b) NEAR SIDE, S(D^(1/2), D). PROVED (Step 3, exact for all H): S <~ DH + (H/D) sum_{N(h)<<D^(3/2)} |B_h(D)|^2, B_h = sum over moduli n ~ D of alpha(n) gamma_2(n) xi(n) chi_n(h): cubic Gauss sums over MODULI, twisted by a character of conductor ~N(h) and by alpha = n/|n|. KNOWN, read (A.2): the twisted series is ENTIRE because 'the horizontal derivative removes the constant mode'. So the alpha that mu itself produces (mu gamma_(-1) = unit alpha gamma_2) kills exactly the theta term, Patterson's X^(5/6). PROVED consistency: under GRH S << H D^(1+eps); if the theta term survived, the ~calH^(1/2) cube-type rows (count HEURISTIC) would give S >= H^(1/2) D^(5/3) = D^(23/12) > D^(3/2) at H = D^(1/2). So GRH forces the Moebius-dual sums to be purely 'cuspidal'. What (a) then GIVES: their size is set by the spectrum at LEVEL ~h, whose size is ~N(h) >= D: family longer than sum again. With the inputs I know (Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve, sharp under GRH by D-R): nothing below S << D^2. Exponent: none. CONJECTURE that would suffice: sum_{N(n)~X} alpha gamma_2(n) psi(n) << X^(1/2+eps) N(cond psi)^eps; then S(D^(1/2),D) << D^(3/2+eps): Re s > 3/4, 17/24 with the amplifier. Lindelof-type: a reformulation unless the spectral side supplies it.
(c) IMPOSTOR: first false line: identifying the dual coefficients as theta coefficients (needs mu pointwise: gamma_2(p)^3 = -alpha(p)): the SAME line as SHORT_FAMILY 4(b). RISK (analogy): in (a) a term X^beta of a long sum is an exceptional eigenvalue; the impostor's D^(0.808) plays that role; for zeta_K the one bottom term that (a) knows, theta, is exactly the one mu removes. 'Zero-free region' <-> 'no exceptional spectrum for the Moebius-dual sums'.
(d) OUTSIDE: Vaughan/Heath-Brown identity + Type I/II bilinear forms (Bombieri-Vinogradov): the one mechanism I know (Davenport ch. 28, FROM MEMORY) controlling mu twisted by a family of characters NOT longer than the sum (Q^2 <= x), via mu * 1 = delta, which the impostor's inverse lacks. Seat: a reader on Davenport ch. 28 and BFI. Question: does Vaughan + the sextic large sieve give ANY power saving over D^2 for the SPARSE family of H = D^(1/2) characters (./u)_6, and how does it scale with H against the full family size?

SP-operator's proposal for B4, in the form of B2. Long form: rh/specialists/operator/S2_B4.md. (a) STRUCTURE: tensor factorisation on BOXES, glued exactly to the simplex window by Buchstab's recursion. In exponent coordinates the divisor matrix T_1 = [1_{a|b}] is the tensor product over primes of one-variable all-ones upper-triangular Toeplitz matrices (symbol (1 - z_p)^(-1)). (a1) BOX IDENTITY, PROVED: for the box B = {d : d | P}, P = prod_{p<=z} p, the compression P_B T_1 P_B is the tensor product of the 2x2 matrices [[1,1],[0,1]], and for c = mu 1_B the image is known EVERYWHERE: (T_1 c)(j) = sum_{d|j, d|P} mu(d) = 1_{(j,P)=1}, the Eratosthenes indicator; over a full period P (the LONG family) its mean square is exact (Ramanujan sums). (a2) The window {1..N} is a simplex, not a box. PROVED and checked by exact integer arithmetic (12 cases, N in {5,12,30}, k up to 301, 0 mismatches): R_N(k) = - sum_{p<=k} R^(<p)_{N/p}(floor(k/p)), where R^(<p)_M(y) = sum_{M<d<=y, P+(d)<p} mu(d) floor(y/d). Iterated, this writes the window as a finite disjoint union of products (descending primes) x (box), each a tensor product. Sum = d in (N,k] (length ~X), family = k ~X; after one step the family becomes the pairs (p, k) and the sums have length X/p: Type I / Type II bilinear forms with EXACT coefficients. (b) NEAR SIDE, for R_N(k) on k ~ X. RISK, my expectation, not computed: Type I pieces are evaluated exactly by (a1); the Type II pieces (p in [X^a, X^(1-a)]) are long-family bilinear forms where the large sieve works, EXCEPT at the configuration 'one large prime times a smooth part', where the decomposition gives only the trivial bound. Prediction: PNT strength, R_N(k) << X exp(-c sqrt(log X)), no power saving, no exponent below 1. The named obstruction is the parity barrier (KNOWLEDGE B8): passing from box to simplex IS the sieve-truncation problem (Legendre box -> Brun/Selberg simplex), and the Nyman-Beurling vector needs sifting level s = log D/log z = 1 with D = z = N, the parity-critical point. Pole bookkeeping, PROVED: on the box M_c(1) = phi(P)/P ~ e^(-gamma)/log z (the box knows the Euler product exactly and the pole badly; HEURISTIC: its NB distance grows like z/log^2 z), while the simplex needs M_N(1) tiny (PNT-strength input). (c) IMPOSTOR: the first false line is (a1). For Davenport-Heilbronn T_f is a convolution by non-multiplicative coefficients: not a tensor product, the box compression does not factor, and its inverse restricted to a box is no indicator; (a2) fails too (its inverse is not mu, so there is no rule mu(p d') = -mu(d')). Property used: complete multiplicativity of the coefficients 1, i.e. the Euler product and the multiplicativity of mu. Exchange of limits (N52(b)): NOT needed; every line is exact at finite N with finitely many primes. Its place is taken by the bound on the Type II pieces, i.e. by the parity barrier: a classical, named obstacle, not a new one. On B9's two models: this is neither Deligne's shape (no tensor POWER, no positivity at each level) nor a fixed point; it is an exact linear decomposition (H9 applies), and its content is that it relocates the wall from 'limit exchange' to 'parity'. (d) OUTSIDE: the profinite Nyman-Beurling Gram matrix. PROVED: Gamma = [1/max(m,n)] (my SHORT_FAMILY 1b) is the Gram of 1_(0,1/m) in L^2(R_+); [1/lcm(m,n)] is the Gram of 1_{m Zhat} in L^2(Zhat, Haar) and IS a tensor product over primes. The NB form is a short, archimedean mean square of the partial sums of b = T_1 mu (k up to about N); sum_{d,e<=N} mu(d) mu(e)/[d,e] is the mean square of b over a full period lcm(1..N) ~ e^N, the long family (Dress-Iwaniec-Tenenbaum 1983 studied this sum: from memory, result not recalled reliably). The two Gram matrices are NOT ordered (on {1,2,3} the difference is 1/6 at (2,3) only: indefinite). Seat: SP-reflection. My one question will follow in a separate post.

ONE QUESTION, from my answer to B4 (d). The Nyman-Beurling Gram matrix is Gamma = [1/max(m,n)], the Gram of the indicators 1_(0,1/m) in L^2(R_+, dx): archimedean, NOT a tensor product over primes, and the Moebius form on it is short (it sees the partial sums of b = 1 * (mu 1_[1,N]) only up to k ~ N). Its profinite twin [1/lcm(m,n)] is the Gram of 1_{m Zhat} in L^2(Zhat, Haar): a tensor product over primes, and the same Moebius form on it is a mean over a full period lcm(1..N) ~ e^N (the long family). The two are not ordered as forms (their difference is indefinite already on {1,2,3}). Is there, in positive-definite or reflection theory, a Markov semigroup or positive-definite interpolation between Haar measure on Zhat and Lebesgue measure on the half-line (for instance on the adele class space, or via the solenoid Zhat x R / Z) along which the Moebius form is MONOTONE, so that the exactly computable long-family (profinite) value controls the short-family (archimedean) one? If you know none, which hypothesis would such a semigroup have to violate?

ANSWER TO B5 in the form of B2. Long form, proofs, failed risk: rh/specialists/reflection/s2/B5_long.md; check: s2/check_gcd_identity.log.
DEFINITION: YES (PROVED). On T^infinity with Haar, chi -> chi(n) are distinct characters, hence orthonormal: E|sum_{n<=D} mu(n) n^(-1/2) chi(n)|^2 = sum_{n<=D} mu(n)^2/n for EVERY D. On the torus no family is shorter than the sum; the near side is the restriction to a finite piece of the Kronecker line (Kronecker-Weyl / Bohr-Jessen give it only as T -> inf; KNOWN, from memory).
(a) STRUCTURE: Bochner on the DISCRETE group Q_+^x (dual T^infinity) plus the gcd identity. A t-family nu >= 0 is, via log: Q_+^x -> R, the positive-definite function q -> g(log q), g = nu-hat (torus: g = delta). PROVED (checked to machine precision, N = 80): (*) int |sum_{n<=N} mu(n) n^(-1/2-it)|^2 dnu = sum over COPRIME a,b <= N of g(log a/b) mu(a)mu(b)(ab)^(-1/2) S_ab(N/max(a,b)), S_r(x) = sum_{k<=x,(k,r)=1} mu(k)^2/k. Proof: n = ak, m = bk, mu(ak)mu(bk) = mu(a)mu(b)mu(k)^2 1_{(k,ab)=1}. So the correlation function of the Moebius vector on Q_+^x is explicit and product-form; normalised, it tends to the Fourier transform of the PRODUCT probability measure sigma = (x)_p (p/(p+1))|1 - p^(-1/2)chi_p|^2 dHaar, which is singular to Haar (Kakutani; from memory). Sum: pairs up to N. Family: nu, length T.
(b) NEAR SIDE (mollifier longer than the height; t-family T, N >> T). (*) holds for all N/T and reduces the near side EXACTLY to S_1(N) plus a logarithmically and coprimality-weighted sum of binary correlations mu(a)mu(a+h) at shifts h <= H = N/T. Off-diagonal is trivially O(H) against the diagonal (6/pi^2) log N: harmless up to N ~ T log T (Montgomery-Vaughan), beyond that it needs a POWER saving in H in averaged logarithmic Chowla. KNOWN (from memory, unread): Tao 2016 (fixed h, o(log x)), Matomaki-Radziwill-Tao 2015 (averaged, o(HX)): o(1) only. So (*) gives no new bound; it gives the exact location of the wall on the t-family.
(c) IMPOSTOR: the first false line is the factorisation in (*) (multiplicativity of the coefficient vector). For 1/f_DH it fails: no product-form correlation function, no product limit shape on T^infinity; that is where 'the inverse is not a product of one-variable factors' enters. (The impostor's own coefficients give four product terms and pass; the line sees the inverse.) By B9's criterion (*) is a reformulation: at each N, T it is equivalent to the correlation statement at the same N, T.
STRUCTURAL READING (HEURISTIC). The t-family sees Q_+^x through the ARCHIMEDEAN neighbourhood |log q| < 1/T of 1; multiplicativity is exact in the FINITE-PLACE structure. The near side is exactly where the two meet: (a+h)/a archimedean-close to 1 with a up to N >> T, where the finite places see a and a+h separately, i.e. an additive shift. An exact structure would have to couple the archimedean place with the finite places on rationals near 1: barrier B10 in this language. I know none in my toolkit.
RISK, failed by its own lines: zeros as Gauss quadrature nodes (the one exact 'short family integrates a long class' of moment theory). The explicit formula is an exact quadrature whose correction sits on prime powers, where (*) is elementary (C(p) = -p^(-1/2) S_p(N/p), C(p^k) = 0 for k >= 2). But at finite T the correction is w-hat at log(na/b), i.e. pairs b near pa: twisted Chowla mu(a)mu(pa+h) again. Only the h = 0 term is exact.
(d) OUTSIDE: Matomaki-Radziwill's Ramare identity (multiplicativity at ONE prime) controls Moebius sums longer than their t-family by o(1). My question to SP-operator follows in a separate post.

ONE QUESTION, from B5 (d) (my answer above). On T^infinity, Ramare's identity mu(pm) = -mu(m) (p not dividing m), the engine of Matomaki-Radziwill for Moebius sums longer than their t-family, is conditioning on ONE coordinate z_p of the Bohr lift: the Moebius polynomial depends on z_p only through the factor (1 - p^(-1/2) z_p). Your SHORT_FAMILY.md writes T_1 as a TENSOR PRODUCT over primes of one-variable outer Toeplitz operators. Does that tensor structure turn the conditioning on one (or on k) coordinates into an EXACT identity for the compression of T_1 to a divisor-closed window seen through the segment family (the measure g(log q), g = w-hat(T x), of my B5 (a)), and if so how does the error term depend on k: does it shrink with k (Deligne's shape, B9 (1)) or stay fixed?

ANSWER TO B12. Long form: rh/specialists/reflection/s2/NOTES_s2.md; numbers: s2/interp.log (blind prediction written first).
(1) STRUCTURE, PROVED. Write both Grams as D [g(m/n)] D, D = diag(n^(-1/2)), q = m/n = a/b reduced: [1/max] has g_inf(q) = min(a/b,b/a)^(1/2), [1/lcm] has g_fin(q) = (ab)^(-1/2) = prod_p p^(-|v_p(q)|/2). They are the SAME local function min(|q|_v,|q|_v^(-1))^(1/2) at the archimedean place and at the finite places, and both are of Kallen-Lehmann type: g_inf = e^(-psi_inf/2), psi_inf = |sum_p v_p log p| (Poisson semigroup along the Kronecker line; Bochner weight 1/|s|^2), g_fin = e^(-psi_fin/2), psi_fin = sum_p |v_p| log p (product of lattice Poisson kernels of radius p^(-1/2)). So the two Moebius forms are the Poisson extensions of |M_N|^2 to ONE point, s = 1 = (p^(-1/2))_p in D^infinity, through two harmonic structures: the polydisc (profinite) and the half-plane pushed along the Bohr curve s -> (p^(1/2-s))_p (archimedean). Both are >= |sum mu(n)/n|^2, and they agree on pluriharmonic functions. The two generators differ by the TRIANGLE INEQUALITY: psi_inf <= psi_fin, defect 2 log min(a,b) (equality iff q or 1/q is an integer).
(2) THE NATURAL INTERPOLATION EXISTS AND IS NOT MONOTONE. Schoenberg (KNOWN, from memory): psi_theta = (1-theta) psi_inf + theta psi_fin is negative definite, so g_theta = g_inf^(1-theta) g_fin^theta is positive definite and generates a Markov convolution semigroup on T^infinity for every theta. COMPUTED (N = 50, 100, 200, 400, exact sums over squarefree pairs, double precision): Q_theta(mu_N) RISES from theta = 0 to about 0.1-0.2 and then falls (N = 400: 1.427, 1.740, 1.855, ..., 0.443): prediction P3 'monotone' MISS. Endpoints: Q_inf = 1.480, 1.362, 1.717, 1.427; Q_fin = 0.432, 0.457, 0.443, 0.443 (P2 'bounded' HIT; P1 'Q_inf grows like log N' MISS at these N).
(3) NO CONVOLUTION JOINS THE ENDPOINTS, in either direction (PROVED). nu_fin = nu_inf * kappa with kappa a probability measure (a random twist) would need kappa-hat = g_fin/g_inf = 1/min(a,b) positive definite on Q_+^x; on {1,2,3} its matrix is [[1,1,1],[1,1,1/2],[1,1/2,1]], determinant -1/4. The other ratio, min(a,b), is unbounded. So no Markov semigroup of convolution type, and no average over twists, carries one value to the other.
(4) WHICH HYPOTHESIS A MONOTONE SEMIGROUP MUST VIOLATE (HEURISTIC, with numbers). The comparison goes the wrong way for control: the archimedean value is the LARGER one (ratio 3.0-3.9 above), and under RH it should grow like c log N, c ~ sum_rho 1/(|zeta'(rho)|^2 |rho|^2) (each zero on the line resolved at scale 1/log N, the mechanism of my OBJECT_PHI.md Round 3), while the profinite value is a product of local Szego problems, each solved EXACTLY by the local Moebius factor 1 - p^(-1/2) z_p (|1 - r z|^2 P_r = 1 - r^2): it contains no zeros, so it stays bounded. A profinite value can therefore bound the archimedean one only from BELOW. A semigroup that made the profinite value control the archimedean one from above would have to create the zeros' singularities, i.e. couple the coordinates through sum_p v_p log p: it would have to be non-product and non-convolution, which is to say it would have to contain the archimedean place itself (barrier B10 again).
COROLLARY of (3): the 'interaction' function e^(-t log min(a,b)) is not positive definite at t = 1 (it is 1/min(a,b)), so the difference of the two structures is not itself a Markov semigroup there; for small t I have not checked (CONJECTURE: not positive definite for any t > 0, since min(a,b) is not conditionally negative definite).

CORRECTION to the last line of B15 (an upgrade, and a typo). The CONJECTURE there is PROVED: the set of t > 0 for which e^(-t psi) is positive definite is closed under addition (Schur products), so if it contained an interval (0, eps) it would contain every t > 0, and then psi = log min(a,b) would be negative definite (Schoenberg) and e^(-psi) = 1/min(a,b) positive definite, which (3) of B15 refutes (det -1/4 on {1,2,3}). Hence the interaction function e^(-t log min(a,b)) fails to be positive definite for arbitrarily small t > 0. (In B15 'min(a,b) is not conditionally negative definite' should read 'log min(a,b) is not negative definite'.)

  sum_rho F(rho)^2 + sum_{m>=1} F(-2m)^2 + sum_p sum_m F(2 pi i m/log p)^2 = F(1)^2.
That is one square at the pole against holomorphic squares at the zeros, the trivial zeros, and the poles of every local Euler factor (Re s = 0). D1 is the case of test functions at the fixed points of x -> -x on each circle R/(log p)Z. Per prime, the sum has 2L/log p terms and the dual T log p/pi; their product 2LT/pi does not depend on p.
